# The open-source register

Every open-source module, standard, open-weights model and speech provider that ThusoIQ Master v3.5 (Gilbert Pulse Engine) names in §15D, §20, §23, §45, with the decision the specification made for it, the engine, routes and doors in this repository it would plug into, and what stands in its way. Sources were checked on 2026-09-14.

**Nothing in this register is adopted.** 34 components are recorded and not one of them is part of MyThuso: no code from any of them is in this repository, no dependency on any of them is declared, and no service calls one. Nothing in this register is adopted until its licence, security, maintenance, data-flow and clinical-use reviews are each recorded.

§15D: open source does not mean production-approved. A module named in a specification is a candidate, and somebody reading its name beside MyThuso's should not come away believing it runs here.

## What MyThuso owns, and no module replaces

| Component | Owner | What it is | Why it is not a module |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gilbert orchestration service** | Akhanya / MyThuso | Conversation state, tool permissions, patient context assembly, care workflow orchestration, escalation, audit and product experience. | No module, framework or model replaces Gilbert's orchestration. §15D calls it the core IP. A module under it can be swapped; the thing that decides which tool a model may call cannot be somebody else's. |
| **Clinical policy & triage** | ThusoIQ | SATS-aligned triage, red-flag rules, Formulary checks, the protocol registry, Sentinel thresholds and human sign-off policy. | No module sets a triage priority, a red-flag rule or a Sentinel threshold. §15D: generative AI may explain; it may not lower a rule-engine priority. The governed SATS and condition protocols remain authoritative. |
| **Sentinel's patient-baseline alerting** | ThusoIQ | Patient-baseline deviation models under MyThuso's clinical protocols, consuming device data through vendor APIs. | No vendor's anomaly-detection framework replaces Sentinel. §45: the alerting logic is the moat MyThuso must own, and the frameworks proposed for it are not licensed to third parties. |

## Procurement rules (§15D)

- **No external component gets direct, unrestricted access to the Health Passport; all access flows through ThusoIQ identity, consent, purpose-of-use and audit controls.** §16: a breach of the record cannot be undone, and every engine already reads it through one gateway. A module is not an exception to that because somebody else wrote it.
- **Open source does not mean production-approved; licence, security, maintenance, dependency, vulnerability, data-flow and clinical-use reviews come before adoption.** A public repository says who can read the code, not who has checked it. Three of the six Momentum repositories have had no commit for more than a year, and one has no licence file at all.
- **Model and provider abstraction is kept from day one: standard request and response schemas, a model registry, feature flags, shadow evaluation and rollback.** §15D: no single model becomes Gilbert. A provider wired straight into a screen is a provider that cannot be withdrawn the day it fails.
- **Patient audio and transcripts are health information when they reveal symptoms or conditions, and get the Passport's data-minimisation, retention, encryption and consent discipline.** A voice describing chest pain is special personal information under POPIA section 26 whichever vendor transcribed it.
- **No internet-search answer becomes clinical advice at runtime; clinical answers are grounded in versioned, governance-approved protocols, Formulary data and patient-specific facts.** §15D: web research is a content-development activity, not the care pathway.
- **Local-language performance is measured with real South African speakers across age, gender, accent, code-switching, noise, low-bandwidth calls, medicine names and emergency phrases before launch.** §15D's launch language gate: marketing support is not the same as clinical readiness.

|---|---|---|---|
| **iFlytek and Baidu acoustic models** | §45 | §45: patient voice is special personal information; routing it through a Chinese cloud model breaches the Passport's data-residency rule and creates sanctions exposure, because several named vendors are on export-control lists. | Instead: open-weights speech models fine-tuned locally with Lelapa AI, Masakhane, the CSIR and university labs on community-recorded data, on the device where possible. |
| **Hikvision and Dahua mmWave radar** | §45 | §45: both carry export-control and security baggage that will fail a scheme's or a government's due diligence. | Instead: radar from neutral mmWave ODMs or Vayyar-class vendors, with all processing on the device and no vendor cloud. |
| **Huawei and Zepp anomaly-detection frameworks** | §45 | §45: those frameworks are not licensed to third parties, and the alerting logic is the moat MyThuso must own. | Instead: Sentinel's own patient-baseline deviation models under MyThuso's clinical protocols, consuming device data through vendor APIs. |

## Doors the links need that do not exist yet

A door a link needs and packages/catalog/feeds.json does not have is written as proposed, with what must be true before it opens, and only for as long as it is absent. A link to a door that does not exist reads as a seam that works. Once the door is declared, the link names it by its real id and its real conditions.

### `wearable-sync`

packages/catalog/apis/devices.json lists it as a door to add: a partner cloud's wearable sync is a supplier callback, not a route. Needed by: Momentum Open Wearables.

- **A data processing agreement exists with every vendor cloud whose data would arrive.** Each one becomes an operator under POPIA section 21 for a reading that may reveal a condition.
- **Every reading is checked against the wearable-readings consent at the moment it arrives.** §5.5: ingestion stops the moment consent is withdrawn, and a batch sync is exactly where that is forgotten.
- **Every reading arrives labelled with its source and as consumer-grade.** A consumer wearable guides conversation and carries no clinical weight or dispatch.

### `hl7v2-inbound`

§26 names POST /hl7v2/inbound, and packages/catalog/apis/record.json holds it as a door to add because the caller is a partner's system. Needed by: OpenHIM, NextGen Connect (Mirth Connect), HL7 Version 2 (ADT, ORU, ORM).

- **Each partner connects over mutual TLS under an agreement that defines its operator role.** §22 and §25: a hospital or a laboratory is a separate responsible party, and a certificate names which one sent a message.
- **Every ADT, ORU and ORM message is mapped to FHIR with Provenance naming the source system before anything is written.** §20: lab-confirmed and self-reported data must always be distinguishable.
- **A message whose patient cannot be matched is held for a person, never matched by a best guess.** A result filed against the wrong patient is two clinical errors at once.

### `model-gateway`

§15D's sixth runtime layer — primary and fallback models, a prompt and model registry, output-schema validation — is declared by no contract in this repository. Needed by: Momentum Notetaker, Reasoning and multimodal language models.

- **At least two models are evaluated and a fallback is named for every task routed to one.** §15D: no single model becomes Gilbert.
- **Every call records the model, prompt and protocol version it ran on.** §15D's audit layer: without the version, a harmful answer cannot be traced or reproduced.
- **A hosted model processes in South Africa, or a section 72 determination names where, under a data processing agreement.** A prompt carrying a patient's symptoms is special personal information in transit.
- **The clinical safety layer runs before any model output reaches a person, and nothing a model returns lowers an urgency.** §15D: allowed actions and minimum urgency are set by rules; the model cannot override downward.

### `nhie-exchange`

§23's fourth integration path registers the Passport with the national exchange as a point-of-service system and matches patients through HPRS. No feed or route declares it. Needed by: OpenHIM, National Health Information Exchange (NHIE / OpenHIM) integration profile, Health Patient Registration System (HPRS).

- **The National Department of Health publishes the integration profile the Passport would conform to, and it is named here.** No official source naming a national exchange or an OpenHIM profile could be found on 14 September 2026; a door built to a guess is the door that is rebuilt.
- **National exchange conformance is passed.** §27's P3 exit criterion.
- **Only the summary set the Department specifies is shared, and no sealed category.** §20: sealed categories are excluded from every grant unless explicitly included.

## What each component refuses

- **Momentum Open Wearables**
  - A reading that came through Open Wearables carries no clinical weight and triggers no dispatch. *Full Scope Engine 9, which the devices contract already refuses on.*
  - Open Wearables does not stand in for the direct adapters for BP cuffs, CGM, SpO₂ or the Thuso Pod. *§15D: keep direct adapters where Open Wearables does not cover the device or the clinical-grade data path.*
- **Momentum FHIR MCP Server**
  - The FHIR MCP Server is never offered to Gilbert as a general-purpose record tool; it is reached as named, read-only tools. *§15D: never expose a generic FHIR CRUD tool directly to the patient-facing model.*
  - A tool it offers that is not on Gilbert's allow-list is refused. *§15D: a restricted, consent-aware tool gateway with an allow-list.*
  - No part of a patient's record is indexed in an external vector store or sent to an external terminology service. *Its README requires Pinecone for document search and calls the LOINC API; either would move special personal information across a border without a section 72 basis.*
- **Momentum HealthStack**
  - A HIPAA-oriented reference stack is not taken as meeting POPIA, South African data residency, key management, disaster recovery or audit requirements. *§15D: do not assume a HIPAA-oriented reference stack is automatically sufficient for South Africa.*
  - No hosting decision follows from HealthStack being written for AWS. *docs/PRIVACY-AND-SECURITY.md records that no residency decision has been made, and a module's defaults are not how one gets made.*
- **Momentum Notetaker**
  - A scribe's draft is never signed by software and never enters the record until a clinician has read, edited and signed it. *§15D: human sign-off policy is owned, and generative AI may explain but not decide.*
  - Consultation audio is never sent to a hosted transcription API; only local mode is considered. *Its README offers the OpenAI API as an option; a consultation's audio is health information under §15D's procurement rules, whichever vendor hears it.*
- **Momentum FHIRBoard**
  - FHIRBoard reads de-identified exports only and never connects to the Passport or any store of identifiable records. *§25: secondary use is de-identified only, with no re-identification.*
  - No governance dashboard shows or exports a row about one person. *§25: never at record level. A dashboard filter narrow enough to find one patient is a record lookup with a chart on it.*
- **Momentum Diagnostipy**
  - Diagnostipy never links to POST /v1/clinical/triage and never produces a priority, a diagnosis or a care setting a person is shown. *§15D: do not treat it as the final diagnostic or triage engine; governed SATS and condition protocols remain authoritative.*
  - No weight or score from Diagnostipy is written into the protocol registry. *packages/catalog/protocols.json refuses a draft carrying any threshold; clinical content comes from the Medical Director and the governance board.*
- **Awesome Health**
  - A project's appearing in Awesome Health is never taken as evidence that it is maintained, safe or fit for clinical use. *§15D: a curated directory, not a runtime platform or an AI Doctor. Its own claim that every link was vetted as active dates from 2023.*
- **HAPI FHIR**
  - A HAPI FHIR server's own REST endpoint is never reachable; only the Passport's gateway talks to it. *§16: there is no code path that reads a record without a grant, a break-glass justification or the patient's own session.*
- **OpenHIM**
  - Nothing says MyThuso is connected to, or conformant with, a national health information exchange. *§27 puts national registration at Release 3, and no published profile exists to conform to.*
- **NextGen Connect (Mirth Connect)**
  - No Mirth Connect release after 4.5.2 is treated as open source. *NextGen's own FAQ: from 4.6 the licence is commercial and proprietary and source is no longer made available.*
  - No HL7 v2 message is written to the record except as FHIR mapped at the gateway, with Provenance. *§23: ADT, ORU and ORM are mapped to FHIR at the gateway.*
- **OpenMRS**
  - MyThuso does not run OpenMRS or OpenEMR as its own record; the Passport is the record. *§16: the Passport is its own module with its own service, store and keys, and no other system holds a copy.*
- **OpenEMR**
  - No OpenEMR code is combined into a MyThuso service; a practice running it is a client of the Passport. *GPL-3.0 would oblige MyThuso to publish the source of the combined work, and the Passport's gateway is the boundary that keeps the two apart.*
- **DICOM**
  - A wound or foot-diary photograph is not presented as diagnostic imaging. *§15D keeps camera use inside the Track A and B claim boundary; DICOM imaging would be a different, regulated service.*
- **Reasoning and multimodal language models**
  - Nothing a model returns lowers a priority the rules set. *§15D: generative AI may explain; it may not lower a rule-engine priority.*
  - A model is never given a general-purpose record tool. *§15D: never expose a generic FHIR CRUD tool directly to the patient-facing model.*
  - No single model or provider becomes Gilbert. *§15D: evaluate at least two, version every model and prompt, and keep a fallback.*
- **Botlhale AI speech APIs**
  - No patient audio is sent to Botlhale AI before a contract and a data processing agreement exist. *§15D: patient audio and transcripts are health information when they reveal symptoms or conditions.*
- **Lelapa AI Vulavula**
  - No patient audio is sent to Lelapa AI before a contract and a data processing agreement exist. *§15D: patient audio and transcripts are health information when they reveal symptoms or conditions.*
- **Global speech and voice stack**
  - No consumer assistant — Google Assistant, Siri or Bixby — becomes Gilbert's voice architecture. *§15D's recommendation: do not make any consumer assistant or single model the architecture.*
- **OpenAI Whisper**
  - The open weights run where MyThuso controls them; a hosted transcription API is not what §45 adopted. *§45: patient voice is special personal information, and open weights give the head start without routing it through somebody else's cloud.*
- **Meta MMS (Massively Multilingual Speech)**
  - MMS is not used in anything MyThuso charges for while its licence is non-commercial. *CC-BY-NC-4.0 forbids commercial use, and a health service a patient pays for is commercial use.*
- **Meta Seamless (SeamlessM4T)**
  - No Seamless model under a non-commercial or custom licence is used in anything MyThuso charges for. *CC-BY-NC-4.0 forbids commercial use, and the custom agreement has not been read by counsel.*
- **HL7 FHIR R4**
  - A resource shaped like FHIR is not called conformant until §26's FHIR validator suite passes. *§26: the Passport ships its own conformance suite, and a hospital integrator will run the validator whether or not MyThuso does.*
- **SMART on FHIR (SMART App Launch)**
  - A SMART scope never stands in for the patient's consent artefact; both are checked on every call. *§21 and §26: the gateway validates the consent artefact on every request, whatever token the caller holds.*
- **HL7 Version 2 (ADT, ORU, ORM)**
  - No integration plan with a South African hospital group or laboratory assumes FHIR alone. *§20: most SA private hospital groups and labs still speak HL7 v2, and the bridge is not optional.*
- **International Patient Summary**
  - A sealed category is left out of the International Patient Summary unless the patient opts it in. *§20 and §24: sealed categories are excluded from the default emergency summary.*
- **SMART Health Links and Cards**
  - The Passport Card is an emergency credential the patient holds, never a credential the state reads. *§45 declined the health-code framing: same outcome, and the framing matters.*
  - Every share link carries a scope, a passcode and an expiry. *§20 and §26: a permanently valid document is a copy of the record nobody can take back.*
- **OpenID Connect**
  - Signing in proves who somebody is and opens no record by itself. *§21: a consent artefact is validated on every request; an identity token is not one.*
- **iFlytek and Baidu acoustic models**
  - No iFlytek or Baidu acoustic model is licensed, called or run for any MyThuso voice. *§45: patient voice is special personal information; routing it through a Chinese cloud model breaches the Passport's data-residency rule and creates sanctions exposure, because several named vendors are on export-control lists.*
- **Hikvision and Dahua mmWave radar**
  - Neither Hikvision nor Dahua supplies a sensor for Ambient Home Mode. *§45: both carry export-control and security baggage that will fail a scheme's or a government's due diligence.*
- **Huawei and Zepp anomaly-detection frameworks**
  - No Huawei or Zepp anomaly-detection framework is licensed; Sentinel's alerting is MyThuso's own. *§45: those frameworks are not licensed to third parties, and the alerting logic is the moat MyThuso must own.*

## What could not be verified

- **Momentum Notetaker** — The README shows an MIT badge and says to see LICENSE, but the repository has no LICENSE file — GitHub's licence API returns 404 and blob/main/LICENSE does not exist — so there is no licence grant to rely on.
- **Lab and PHR components** — §15D names a category rather than a component, so there is no repository, licence or activity to read until somebody shortlists one.
- **Reasoning and multimodal language models** — §15D names no model and requires at least two to be evaluated, so there is no provider to look up until a shortlist exists.
- **Global speech and voice stack** — §15D names no vendor for the fallback, so there is nothing to look up until one is chosen.
- **Google's African-language speech work** — §45 does not name a model or dataset. The most plausible open resource, the WAXAL dataset, is licensed CC-BY-4.0 or CC-BY-SA-4.0 by data provider and lists no South African language; if the sentence meant another Google model, no licence was verified for it.
- **HL7 Version 2 (ADT, ORU, ORM)** — HL7's product page and its free-IP FAQ answered with a web-application-firewall challenge and no content, so neither the current version nor the terms could be read.
- **IHE XDS.b and MHD** — The XDS.b page carries only an IHE International copyright notice, and a CC0 badge was reported on the MHD guide without its wording being seen, so the terms of use are not recorded.
- **International Patient Summary** — The HL7 guide's licence wording was not seen directly, and ISO's pages for ISO 27269 returned 403; the IPS editorial team states the ISO standard is not free.
- **National Health Information Exchange (NHIE / OpenHIM) integration profile** — No National Department of Health source naming an NHIE or an OpenHIM integration profile could be found: the 2014 Health Normative Standards Framework (Gazette 37583) calls for a health information exchange without naming one, and the 2019–2024 digital health strategy and the 2026–2027 performance plan do not mention one.
- **Health Patient Registration System (HPRS)** — Only planning documents describe HPRS — the 2026–2027 performance plan reports it installed at 3,266 health establishments by March 2025 — and no specification, interface or terms of use were found.
- **iFlytek and Baidu acoustic models** — Declined by §45; nothing about these vendors was looked up, because nothing from them will be used.
- **Hikvision and Dahua mmWave radar** — Declined by §45; nothing about these vendors was looked up, because nothing from them will be used.
- **Huawei and Zepp anomaly-detection frameworks** — Declined by §45; nothing about these frameworks was looked up, because §45 records that they are not licensed to third parties.

## The register's own rules

- **Nothing in this register is adopted until its licence, security, maintenance, data-flow and clinical-use reviews are each recorded.** §15D: open source does not mean production-approved. A module named in a specification is a candidate, and somebody reading its name beside MyThuso's should not come away believing it runs here.
- **A licence, a URL or a date of last activity is recorded as it was read from the primary source on a stated day, or it is null with the reason it could not be read.** A guessed licence is how copyleft code ends up inside a product that cannot publish its source, and a guessed URL is how a typo-squatted package gets installed.
- **No module reaches the record engine except through the Passport's consent gateway.** §15D's first procurement rule, and §16's design test: if a module were compromised, it must not hold the records.
- **A module driven by a model reads the record only through Gilbert's allow-listed tools, and never writes to it.** §15D: never expose a generic FHIR CRUD tool directly to the patient-facing model. A write tool in front of a model is a record anybody can edit by typing.
- **Nothing registered as a prototype, a pilot or a reference links the triage route.** §15D: Diagnostipy is for prototypes and test harnesses, and clinical policy and triage are owned. A weighted score that reaches the triage route is a diagnosis nobody governs.
- **A vendor the specification declined is linked to no engine, route or door, and is never adopted.** §45 records why each was declined so the decision is auditable. A link would be the first step of reversing it without anybody deciding to.
- **No package manifest in this repository declares a registered component.** Adoption starts with the five reviews. A dependency added to try something is adoption that skipped them, and it is found by the build rather than by an audit.
- **A door a link needs and packages/catalog/feeds.json does not have is written as proposed, with what must be true before it opens, and only for as long as it is absent.** A link to a door that does not exist reads as a seam that works. Once the door is declared, the link names it by its real id and its real conditions.
- **What MyThuso owns is never marked replaceable, and no component is registered as replacing it.** §15D: own the patient experience, clinical policy, orchestration, safety, data model and audit trail; rent or replace what sits underneath.

Held by the "open-source register" section of `scripts/check-boundaries.mjs`. Refused vendors: iFlytek and Baidu acoustic models; Hikvision and Dahua mmWave radar; Huawei and Zepp anomaly-detection frameworks.
